title: The Rape of the Daughters of Leucippus by Peter Paul Rubens
episode: Rubens, The Rape of the Daughters of Leucippus
description: Rubens’s swirling scene from Greek myth of the twins Castor and Pollux carrying off two sisters on rearing horses, painted around 1618. It is one of more than 60 Rubens paintings in the Alte Pinakothek.

title: Madame de Pompadour by François Boucher
description: Boucher’s full-length portrait of Louis XV’s official mistress in 1756, surrounded by books, a writing desk, and sheet music to show her learning and influence. It is in the Alte Pinakothek.

title: The Sin by Franz von Stuck
description: Stuck’s dark, sensual painting of Eve with a huge serpent around her shoulders, a sensation in Munich in 1893. He made several versions, and one hangs in the altar he built for it in his own villa.

title: I Lock My Door Upon Myself by Fernand Khnopff
episode: Khnopff, I Lock My Door Upon Myself
description: A dreamlike painting by the Belgian Symbolist Khnopff of a woman lost in thought, titled after a poem by Christina Rossetti. It belongs to the Neue Pinakothek, which is closed for renovation.
